chunks: And by this chain, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It was from his supplications that he would say: O Light! O Holy! O First of the foremost and O Last of the latter! O Beneficent! O Merciful! Forgive me the sins that change the bounties, and forgive me the sins that bring down calamities, and forgive me the sins that rupture the defences, and forgive me the sins that bring down afflictions, and forgive me the sins that assist the enemies, and forgive me the sins that hasten perishing, and forgive me the sins that cut off hope, and forgive me the sins that darken the atmosphere, and forgive me the sins that uncover the cover, and forgive me the sins that repel supplication, and forgive me the sins that repel the rain of the sky.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific sins that remove divine blessings according to Imam al-Sadiq's supplication?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs the divine names 'Al-Nur' and 'Al-Quddus' to emphasize Allah's purity and light as the source of all blessings. It reflects the Shia theological concept of 'sabr al-shukr' (patience in prosperity) and 'sabr al-niqmah' (patience in adversity), linking specific sins to tangible cosmic consequences like withheld rain and veiled defenses. This narrative underscores the causal link between spiritual state and material reality, a theme central to Shia devotional practice.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said:

‘It was from his<sup>asws</sup> supplications, that he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘O Light! O Holy! O First of the foremost ones and O Last of the latter ones! O Beneficent! O Merciful! Forgive for me the sins which change the Bounties, and Forgive for me the sins which bring down the calamities, and Forgive for me the sins which rupture the defences, and Forgive for me the sins which bring down the afflictions, and Forgive for me the sins which assist the enemies, and Forgive for me the sins which hasten the perishing, and Forgive for me the sins which cut-off the hopes, and Forgive for me the sins which darken the atmosphere, and Forgive for me the sins which uncover the cover, and Forgive for me the sins which repel the supplications, and Forgive for me the sins which repel the rains of the sky’’.
en.sarwar: 29. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

O light, O Holy, O the First of the beings in the beginning, O the Last of the beings of the later times, O the Beneficent, O the Merciful, forgive my such sins that change the bounties, forgive my such sins that bring in misfortunes, forgive my such sins that crush the protections, forgive my such sins that send down evil conditions, forgive my such sins that assist the enemy, forgive my such sins that hasten destruction, forgive my such sins that cut off hope, forgive my such sins that darken the space, forgive my such sins that remove the cover and grace, forgive my such sins that repulse the prayer and forgive my such sins that turn away the rain from the sky.”
